note: Two readers share this file: `scripts/replay-goldens.ts` (TypeScript, live model replay) and `packages/ai/test/meal_description_goldens_test.dart` (Dart, stub golden runner). Keeping one list means a drift between them is impossible — two answers to 'is this Egyptian' is worse than one.
matching: A term matches only at a word boundary: start of string or a space before, and space/end/،/./(/) after. An optional Arabic conjunction و may sit directly in front of the term. NO OTHER PREFIX is optional — بيحتوي is Egyptian and must never count as the Modern Standard يحتوي.
history: Both rules in `matching` are corrections, not design. The conjunction was not optional until 2026-08-05, so وتعتبر went unreported twice in the version 1 replay of meal-analysis — once carrying a whole fixture's verdict of 'Modern Standard markers: none'. And the entry for الكوك was the other way round until the same day: it flagged الطباخ and named الكوك as the fix, which the founder had settled in the opposite direction on 2026-08-04 (ADR-0010), so from meal-analysis version 2 on it would have flagged every correct reply. A check that is confidently wrong is worse than one that is silent, which is the whole reason this data has tests of its own.

msa.note: Egyptian: فراخ — named in the prompt
Egyptian: رز — named in the prompt
Egyptian: طماطم — named in the prompt

possessives: بتاع and بتاعة were the only members of the possessive family until 2026-08-06, and the word-boundary rule means neither matches بتاعي — which is what a Cook actually writes. Five of eight drafts in the first meal-description replay were reported as 'Egyptian markers: none' while carrying بتاعي, بتاعتي, بعملها or معموله. The detector was under-reporting the dialect it exists to find, and a register check that can only say 'none' certifies what it cannot see. بيتقدم is NOT here on purpose: it is menu voice, the register the prompt rules out in the same breath as Modern Standard, so filing it under Egyptian markers would make the detector approve the thing it should flag.
